html:
Jacobo Árbenz was the president of Guatemala from 1951 to 1954. His land reform, which took unused land from large estates and from the United Fruit Company, led to his overthrow in a coup organised by the CIA.

An army officer, he was a leader of the October Revolution of 1944 and defence minister under Arévalo. Elected president in 1950, he passed Decree 900 in 1952, which gave land to about half a million people. The United Fruit Company, the largest landowner, lost much of its idle land, and was paid compensation based on the low value it had declared for tax.

The United States, seeing the hand of communists in his government, armed rebels and ran a campaign of fear. He resigned in June 1954 in the coup and lived in exile until his death in Mexico. Guatemala formally apologised to his family in 2011. His fall opened the way to the civil war in Guatemala.
